reach.rationale: No experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs at all, but the entire app rests on TanStack Start, which only reached 1.0 stable on 2026-10-13 (two weeks ago), plus srvx 1.0 (Sep 2026) and TypeScript 7 (Jul 2026) — recently-stable APIs in central places, which is exactly the anchor-3 case.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokedex.functions.ts:8-27 — all server functions (the Start-specific surface) live in one module
app/src/lib/pokedex.server.ts:1-40 — server-only API access and caching isolated behind one module
app/server.mjs:1-16 — all srvx usage confined to a single 16-line entry file
app/src/routes/__root.tsx:14 — only non-contained touch: reads the private match._notFound property
containment.rationale: Everything swappable (srvx server, server-function layer, cache) is isolated behind single modules, and the Start idioms spread across routes are the framework's mandatory core. The single line reaching into a private router property keeps this from a 5.

evidence: app/package.json:6 — Start itself is mandated by SPEC.md, pinned to the current stable line

app/src/lib/pokedex.functions.ts:8 — createServerFn().validator() is the documented pattern for keeping HTTP fetching server-side (loaders are isomorphic), matching the official start-core/server-functions skill
app/server.mjs:5-16 — srvx serves the built Start handler the same way TanStack's own examples do; nothing here a plainer stable stack could do better
app/vite.config.ts:5 — no RSC, no betas, no flags: deliberately avoids the framework's still-bleeding-edge features
justification.rationale: Every recently-stable choice buys something a stable alternative couldn't (spec-mandated framework, type-safe server functions, the framework authors' own prod-server recipe), and the tempting experimental surface (RSC, canary flags) was deliberately left untouched.

findings.issue: Root head() reads match._notFound, an underscore-prefixed private Router property, to pick the not-found title (the public match.status === 'notFound' half of the check is fine).
findings.suggestion: Rely on match.status alone, or set the not-found title via the notFoundComponent/head of a dedicated catch-all route instead of probing private match internals.

findings.issue: The generated route tree is committed even though TanStack's file-based routing guidance puts routeTree.gen.ts in .gitignore (app/.gitignore lists .tanstack/ but not the generated tree).
findings.suggestion: Add src/routeTree.gen.ts to .gitignore and let the build regenerate it; committed generated code can drift from the route files.

summary: The app contains zero experimental, preview or canary APIs — no unstable_ names, no experimental build flags, and no RSC opt-in. Its recency risk is concentrated where the spec forces it: the whole app sits on TanStack Start, which only hit 1.0 stable on 2026-10-13, with srvx 1.0 and TypeScript 7 as the other recently-stable pieces, all pinned to current stable lines and isolated behind clean module boundaries. Only real nits are one line touching a private Router property and a committed generated route tree.
